Their Theorems 1--2 give entrywise Gaussian inference and a matching scalar instance-wise lower bound under row- and column-side subblock conditioning, signal-to-noise and noise restrictions, and target-local leverage conditions, without this note's global-incoherence condition. This note instead imposes a single low-rank structure on \(L\) and permits arbitrary \(D\) supported on \(W\), so neither full class contains the other and no constructive upper bound transfers. Converse transfer to their realized-data class requires a separate embedding that fixes \(N^\star\) across the hypercube while varying \(M^{\star,\epsilon}=L^\epsilon\).
Theorems 1 and 4 derive nuclear detection boundaries and nuclear-diameter rank-adaptation impossibility in Gaussian trace regression.
Theorems 3.4--3.5 characterize worst-case Frobenius residual error for nuclear-norm minimization with one missing block.

project_justification.gap: Yan and Wainwright impose separate low-rank structures on \(M^\star\) and \(N^\star\), with no joint structure between them. This note instead imposes a single low-rank structure on the untreated matrix \(L\) and permits an arbitrary treatment-effect matrix \(D\) supported on \(W\). The note's realized treated mean \(L+D\) therefore need not be low rank, while Yan--Wainwright's low-rank matrices need not satisfy this note's known-rank, strong-factor, or global-incoherence restrictions; neither full class contains the other. Their scalar theory uses row- and column-side subblock conditioning, signal-to-noise and noise restrictions, and target-local leverage conditions, but not this note's global-incoherence condition. Thus no constructive upper bound transfers across the full classes, and converse transfer to their richer realized-data experiment requires a separate fixed-\(N^\star\) embedding. More broadly, sharp staggered-panel inference remains coordinatewise or functional-specific, whereas global matrix confidence theory uses random or isotropic measurements; no located result gives this note's tuple-indexed honest nuclear ball under a deterministic adoption wedge together with both the fixed-interior frontier and the saturated-incoherence boundary characterization.

prose_updates.related_work: Yan and Wainwright provide the closest computational and inferential comparison. Their setup imposes separate low-rank structures on \(M^\star\) and \(N^\star\), with no joint structure between them. This note instead imposes a single low-rank structure on \(L\) and permits arbitrary supported \(D\), so the realized treated mean \(L+D\) need not be low rank; conversely, their low-rank matrices need not obey this note's known-rank, strong-factor, or global-incoherence restrictions. Hence neither full class contains the other. Their four-block SVD theory gives non-asymptotic entrywise Gaussian approximations and matching scalar lower bounds under row- and column-side subblock conditioning, signal-to-noise and noise restrictions, and target-local leverage conditions. No constructive upper bound transfers across the full classes. For a converse comparison in Yan--Wainwright's richer realized-data experiment, one must separately fix \(N^\star\) across the hypercube and vary only \(M^{\star,\epsilon}=L^\epsilon\); in this note's tuple notation this means taking \(D^\epsilon=N^\star-L^\epsilon\) on \(W\). The present \(D^\epsilon=0\) proof is an observed-law lower bound and does not itself furnish that richer-experiment embedding. Bai and Ng supply the tall-wide factor-rotation architecture and asymptotic counterfactual expansions under strong observed subblocks; block transport is used here as a supporting identification lemma. Carpentier and Nickl supply testing reductions for honest nuclear confidence diameter in isotropic Gaussian trace regression, with rank adaptation as their central obstruction. Capponi and Stojnic analyze worst-case Frobenius residuals for nuclear-norm minimization with one missing block, a procedure-specific target distinct from the uniformly honest radius. Chen, Fan, Ma, and Yan study debiased uncertainty quantification under random sampling, where sampling isometry replaces deterministic block geometry. Chatterjee characterizes qualitative recoverability under arbitrary deterministic masks, and Arkhangelsky and Imbens organize factor and assignment-pattern distinctions without a global honest matrix radius. Against these comparators, Theorem \ref{thm:balanced-frontier} supplies the fixed-\(\mu>1\) interior \(\sigma\sqrt n\) frontier, whereas Theorem \ref{thm:boundary-frontier-obstruction} shows for every \(0<\kappa\le1\) that the \(\mu=1\) frontier is only order \(\sigma\), or exactly zero at the known-level elbow, despite an order-\(\sigma\sqrt n\) unrestricted tangent modulus. Xia, Yan, and Wainwright and Farias, Li, and Peng remain functional-specific benchmarks; the ATT proposition claims coverage transfer and no optimal-length comparison.
